explanation:
The hypothesis is right except for one cell in pair 1: at (5,9) the 4-plus and the 7-block overlap and the output keeps the 4. My stamping order (ascending colour) let 7 overwrite it. The 4 motif sits above the 7 motif in the left panel, so I stamp motifs from the bottom of the left panel upward, which leaves the topmost motif on top in any overlap. That fixes pair 1 and leaves pairs 2 and 3 untouched.

## Worked solution

**What the grid is made of.** A full vertical divider line (colour 2, 3 or 1 – it varies, so I read it with `dividers`) separates two parts. The left part is a legend of small motifs on background 0: a plus, an X, a 3x3 block, a diagonal, a T, etc., each of one colour. The right part is a rectangular frame: a border of one dominant colour (3, 4, 2, 9, 1 ...) with a few marker cells of other colours on it, and an empty interior. The markers come in matching pairs: a colour that appears on the top border also appears at the same column on the bottom border, and a colour on the left border reappears at the same row on the right border. So every marker colour defines some marker rows and some marker columns.

**How the output is built.** For each motif colour in the legend that has both a marker row and a marker column, the motif is stamped into the frame, centred on each (marker row, marker column) crossing: pair 1 stamps the 4-plus at row 4/col 9 and the 7 block at row 6/col 10; pair 2 stamps the 7-T at rows 2,7 × cols 7,11 (four copies) and the 5-X at row 5/col 9; pair 3 stamps the 3-plus at row 3/col 7 and the 6-X at row 6/col 11. The stamped motif is then erased from the legend. A motif whose colour has no marker pair stays in the legend untouched (the 8 diagonal in pair 2, the 7 bar in pair 3 – colour 7 marks only columns there, not rows). When two stamps overlap (pair 1, cell (5,9)), the motif that is higher in the legend wins, so I paint from the bottom motif upward.

**Test inputs.** Test 1 (divider 3, frame colour 9): the 1-plus goes to rows 3,12 × col 7 (two copies), the 4-diagonal to row 7/col 14, the 6-block to row 9/col 15; the 7 motif has no row marker and stays; the 8 marker has no motif. Test 2 (divider 2, frame colour 1): the 7-T goes to row 2 × cols 8,10, the 4 motif to row 5/col 13, the 6-diagonal to row 8/col 14; the 8 bar stays in the legend. In both tests two stamps touch, and the upper legend motif is painted last so it stays on top.
